news.headline: Oracle falls 2.8% as Nvidia news cools the AI cloud rebound
news.summary: Oracle gave back part of its prior-day gain on November 12 as Nvidia-related news weighed on AI infrastructure names. Separately, the Texas data-center construction debate keeps Oracle in focus as one of the most exposed AI builders.

news.headline: Oracle jumps about 9% as CoreWeave's funding reset eases AI debt fears; Bernstein keeps $325 target
news.summary: Oracle rose roughly 8.8% on November 11, adding about $31.6 billion in market value, after CoreWeave's results and refinancing eased worries about AI infrastructure debt. Bernstein reiterated Outperform with a $325 target, arguing the selloff undervalues the data-center and database businesses.

news.headline: Oracle breaks ground on its Nashville world headquarters campus
news.summary: Oracle held the groundbreaking for its River North headquarters campus in Nashville, designed by Foster + Partners and targeted for completion by end-2031, with public open-house events on Nov 12-14. The ceremony came the same day the stock jumped about 9% as CoreWeave's beat-and-raise quarter eased AI-infrastructure funding fears.

news.headline: Why Oracle Stock Is Up Today
news.summary: Oracle shares jumped roughly 9% intraday on Nov 11 to around $128 as AI cloud stocks rebounded, bouncing off the two-year low of about $109 set on Nov 6. Benzinga also pointed to a record peak-demand reduction by Oracle's Opower utility software, though the move looked mostly like a sector-wide relief rally.

news.headline: Bernstein Reiterates Outperform on Oracle's AI Growth
news.summary: Bernstein's Mark Moerdler kept Oracle as a top pick with an Outperform rating and $325 target after updating his 10-year model, arguing both the AI data-center unit and the core database business are AI winners. He said Oracle should not need further funding and is about 18 months from positive free cash flow, naming OpenAI's IPO and the FCF turn as catalysts.

news.headline: Ezra Klein Floats “the End of Oracle” as OpenAI Weighs Smaller Data Center Plans
news.summary: Citing a Wall Street Journal report, TIKR says senior OpenAI leaders were discussing whether to reset next year's data-center capacity expectations after the US elections. With S&P estimating OpenAI at about half of Oracle's $664B backlog, any cut would hit OCI growth most directly, and the mid-December Q2 report will show whether the backlog held.

catalysts.label: Annual Meeting of Stockholders
catalysts.detail: Virtual annual meeting at 9:00 a.m. CT on November 18, 2026 (announced November 6); replay on the IR site through November 25.

catalysts.label: Fiscal Q2 2027 earnings
catalysts.detail: Projected date (calendar estimates range from about Dec 10 to Dec 14 after the close); not yet confirmed by Oracle, which usually sets the date in late Nov/early Dec. Company guide: revenue $21.00-21.64B, non-GAAP EPS $1.83-1.91. First print after Investor Day and the $20B raise; focus on RPO/backlog after the Tencent cancellation, OCI growth, capex and cash burn against the reaffirmed FY27 guide of $90B+ revenue and $8.10 non-GAAP EPS.

catalysts.label: Project Jupiter power resolution
catalysts.detail: Whether the force-majeure situation at the $165B New Mexico campus is resolved and power/permitting issues are cleared; delays here push out OpenAI-linked capacity and revenue recognition.

catalysts.label: Fiscal Q3 2027 earnings
catalysts.detail: Expected mid-March 2027 based on Oracle's usual calendar; next checkpoint on capacity ramp and progress toward the FY27 targets.

catalysts.label: Free cash flow turns positive (company target)
catalysts.detail: Investor Day target: FCF positive in the second half of FY28 and at least $30B in FY29, with net debt below 3.5x adjusted EBITDA in FY29 and growth self-funded from then on. Any slippage would likely force funding beyond the $20B cap, which is already fully used.

pulse: As of Nov 12, Oracle has bounced roughly 9% to about $128 after CoreWeave's strong quarter eased fears over AI-infrastructure financing, recovering from a two-year low near $109 on Nov 6 when it briefly traded below the $116 price of its $20B equity-and-debt raise. Sell-side support remains firm (Bernstein Outperform/$325, KeyBanc Overweight/$300), but the Microsoft capacity wind-down, the abandoned Tencent chip-leasing deal and the ~$95B capex bill keep funding risk in focus. Next up are the Nov 18 annual meeting and fiscal Q2 2027 results around Dec 10, where RPO conversion and cash burn versus the Investor Day path to positive free cash flow in 2028 will be tested.
